appraisal_events.evidence: « Pour l'agrément qu'elle vous apportera ! On la laisse dans son coin. Du reste, elle est un peu gaga. »
appraisal_events.explanation: Unnamed guests at Gilberte's party openly dismiss the elderly Odette within earshot as senile and not worth attending to, excluding her from valued regard even as the hostess's mother.

appraisal_events.evidence: « elle était devenue... infiniment sympathique ; car elle qui avait trompé Swann et tout le monde, c'était l'univers entier qui maintenant la trompait ; et elle était devenue si faible qu'elle n'osait même plus... se défendre contre les hommes. »
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator declares that the once-deceptive Odette has paradoxically become genuinely sympathetic now that she is deceived and defenseless in turn, a moral/emotional gain bound to a loss of her former worldly power.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Tu te trompes, j'ai cherché dans le Gotha de cette année, me confessa naïvement Bloch... marié à Sidonie, duchesse de Duras, née des Baux. »
appraisal_events.explanation: Bloch's confident genealogical research into the Gotha turns out to be a naive misidentification of the new princesse de Guermantes, and the narrator's phrasing ('me confessa naïvement') gently exposes his lack of real social sophistication.

status_effects.explanation: She is openly written off and excluded from valued attention by fellow guests who mock her as senile.
Despite her loss of former power, the narrator reassesses her as newly and genuinely sympathetic, a positive moral shift even as she becomes more vulnerable.
His confidently asserted genealogical claim is exposed as a naive error, undercutting his pretension to real social knowledge.

ambiguities: The passage also contains brief, oblique evaluative touches on other candidates (e.g., the narrator's aside that 'Charlus ne vaut guère mieux' than the dead Swann, and the elegiac description of the deceased former princesse de Guermantes as dispossessed by succession) that were judged too essayistic or fragmentary to support a discrete local event under the smallest-sufficient-reading standard.
